_what: TRN-001 reproduction blockout spec (round 1: camera + blockout). Generic prayer-room feature wall; dims are the 2026-07-30 study's mutually-consistent spine (vault-grounded where the vault speaks, trade standards where it is silent). Committed file carries TRN-id + generic content only per qa/reproduction-curriculum.md.

room._height: 2026-08-01, ROUND 11. The room is 105 mm taller than nine rounds assumed, and the error was invisible because nothing in the model disagreed with anything else in the model. Found by a fleet sweep of regions nobody had looked at, then attacked: three independent detectors put the target's unit-top arris at z=2773 on the header face plane (2773.5+/-0.3 and 2773.4+/-0.3 from two edge-finders whose controls reproduce our own known 2700 to 2 mm; a third, cruder one failed its control at -32 mm but agreed on the OFFSET at +66 mm against the others' +73, which is what a common-mode bias does). THE CEILING ITSELF IS A SEPARATE NUMBER and the first claim conflated them: back-projecting a top edge onto an ASSUMED header setback trades ceiling height against header depth. Closed with an instrument containing no header at all -- the left side wall is a plane x=Xw, its FLOOR junction fixes Xw because z=0 is known, and its CEILING junction then gives Zc, both lines constrained to the wall-normal vanishing point so plank seams cannot win. Control on our own render: Xw -1818.5+/-0.8 against the model's -1815.0 and Zc 2702.9+/-0.6 against 2700. Target: Zc 2805+/-5. Forcing Zc=2773 would require the target's floor line to be wrong by 13.7 px where the control's error is 0.6 px. So: ceiling 2805, header top 2773 (the band HANGS 32 mm below the ceiling, it does not touch it), header depth 93 (its visible soffit band is 14.0 px in the target against our 15.0). The band's BOTTOM arris barely moves -- 2439 -> 2430 -- which is why every landmark fit stayed happy: the edge the solve could see was already right and the edge it could not see was 73 mm out.

light._what: 2026-07-31 round 4 (LIGHT). Every knob here is either a MEASUREMENT off the target or a declared inference — see downlights._measured. The round opened on trn001_lightcheck numbers, not on a look: our ceiling read 1.21x the wall against the target's 0.73x, our cubbies 1.63x too bright, our blacks 2.7x lifted, our frame's p99/p1 range 66:1 against 141:1, and our halo 1.92x too strong while clipping 2.15% of the frame against 0.08%. All five are one defect — rounds 1-3 lit the set with a WORLD, which lights a ceiling exactly as hard as a floor.
light._kelvin: 6000 K is a MEASUREMENT, bracketed at 5200/6200 against the target's own white surfaces: at 5200 our white wall read R/G 1.111 B/G 0.907 against the target's 1.050/0.951, at 6200 it read 1.060/0.976. The room still looks warm because the WOOD warms it, which is also why the target's ceiling (1.21/0.81, lit only by bounce off floor and header) is warmer than its walls (1.05/0.95) — our 3800 K first cut made every white surface in the room orange.
light._halo_w: bracketed against the glow band's ratio to the wall, not against how bright it looks: 16 gave 2.14x, 13 gave 2.22x, target is 1.72x. Pushing the strip deeper into the recess (setback 16 -> 45) was TESTED and moved it 2.223 -> 2.191, i.e. the halo's geometry is not the lever, its power is.

world._what: the world is not this room's light source — with the box closed it is only what leaks in. Rounds 1-3 ran it at 0.55 doing ALL the work, which is what made our ceiling as bright as our walls.

film._exposure: set so the two frames' MEDIANS agree (1.05). This is not a look decision: trn001_lightcheck refuses to trust its own absolute column unless the medians are within 5%, and until now they were not, so every absolute reading the lane took was exposure-contaminated and only the rel ladder was usable -- a ladder normalised by wall_bay_right, which a wall-wash moves. Matching the medians is what makes the wall-wash measurable at all.

light._fill_refuted: 2026-07-31: an AREA light standing off frame on the camera side — the room's door/window — was BUILT and REFUTED by measurement, not by taste. The reasoning that led to it still stands (the target's floor ramps 42% toward frame-right while its ceiling shows no lean and its wall is brighter at the BOTTOM, which no ceiling fixture produces), but the source itself flattens the frame instead of ramping it: p99/p1 fell 50 -> 28 at 150 W and -> 15 at 400 W, while the floor tilt it was meant to create fell 21.7% -> 15.1% -> 7.1%. Recorded as an unresolved measurement like round 2's surround, NOT iterated (R1).

downlights._measured: RE-DERIVED 2026-08-01 and the old value was internally inconsistent with its own spec. The recorded x -999.5/+1164.7 at y -605.0/-605.5 is not reproducible from the two lens discs at ANY ceiling height: at 2700 they back-project to (-904.9,-769.2) and (+1143.7,-767.9). The 'both 605 mm off the wall to within 0.5 mm' evidence was also VACUOUS as a height argument -- two ceiling lamps in one row are coplanar in y at every candidate ceiling for this camera (|dy| 1.32 mm at 2700, 1.41 at 2805), so that agreement could never have selected a height, only confirmed they are a row. At the measured ceiling of 2805 the same disc pixels give x -1077.8 / +1117.4 at y -521.7. WHAT THIS COSTS ROUND 9: the wall-wash was argued from '605 mm off the wall on a 2700 ceiling, which is what a wall-wash row is'. The real setback is 522 mm under a 2805 ceiling -- a TIGHTER wash, so the mechanism's direction survives and its bracketed 7 degrees must be re-bracketed against the new geometry rather than assumed to carry over.
downlights._beam: THE PROFILE WAS CHOSEN BY MEASUREMENT, from three real LM-63 files. Every remaining error after the level was right said one thing — our wall was over-washed — so the beam was too wide. 5.ies (Halo R-30 flood, 141 cd still at 40 deg) washed the wall from above and gave it the WRONG vertical shape; 30.IES (Kurt Versen C7394, medium) was better but flattened the frame to 32:1; 29.IES (Kurt Versen C7302, a real tight downlight, zero output past 45 deg) fixed four independent readings at once — cubby 0.051 vs 0.062 target, header 0.231 vs 0.252, the wall's top-to-bottom gradient flipped to the target's own shape, and the floor's falloff went 5.1% -> 23.6% against the target's 37.6%.
downlights._wallwash: 2026-08-01, owner order (1): TAKE LIGHT OFF THE FLOOR RATHER THAN ADD A SOURCE. Three knobs, measured together at the quick rung across 22 configs, and each earns its place on a different reading. (a) tilt_deg 7: the row is 605 mm off the wall and downlight_positions already calls that 'what a wall-wash row is', but every round so far emitted it at nadir, which is why our floor field was explained by distance-to-nearest-lamp at R2 0.756-0.965 while the target's reaches 0.019. Fitted in world millimetres, the depth gradient goes +0.762/m -> +0.213/m against the target's +0.308/m. Tilt is the ONLY lever tried in this lane that lowers a horizontal and raises a vertical in one move, because it adds nothing. Bracketed 0/4/7/10/14.8/17/19.8/29.2/51.5 deg: past ~10 it overshoots the wall (1.13x) and the marble (1.14x), which were the two patches nadir already had right. (b) ies 5.ies: _beam_retest measured this profile as better on aggregate (3.48 -> 2.13) and SHELVED it because it broke header/plinth/cubby -- exactly the three patches the wall-wash tilt feeds. Neither half works alone; the pair does. (c) watt 45 / fill_watt 45: moving power from the measured row (which sits over the one floor patch reading 2.18x) to the inferred rows (which feed floor_near, reading 0.63x). fill_watt is INFERRED and this raises it, so it is declared the softest of the three. RESULT, absolute and exposure-matched so the comparison is legitimate: aggregate |abs-1| 2.98 -> 1.71, worst patch 1.18 -> 0.33, patch_range 38.7 -> 26.4 against the target's 27.6, and every one of the twelve ladder patches moved toward the target, none away.

light._cove_refuted: 2026-08-01, R1 STOP on the room-light mechanism — SECOND attempt, refuted like the first but for a reason worth keeping. A concealed cove wall-wash was built (hidden behind the header soffit at y=-72, z=2412, aimed down the wall) because the repaired instrument said our verticals run 0.78x while our horizontals run 1.11x (ceiling) and 2.20x (far floor), with the wall's own ramp 1.81 against the target's 1.40. It DID what it was built to do — verticals 0.779 -> 1.023 at 48W/55W, i.e. onto the target's 1.00 — and it failed everything else at the same time: ceiling 1.11 -> 1.25, far floor barely moved (2.20 -> 2.13), and p99/p1 fell 56 -> 54. Four configurations, one shape of result: horizontals worsen as verticals improve, which by the fix list's own wording is 'a trade, not a cure'. AND THE GATING TEST IS UNSATISFIABLE BY THIS LANE, which is the part to remember: it requires p99/p1 to RISE, p1 is the darkest 1% of the frame, 93.2% of the target's darkest 1% lives inside the two cubby stacks, and substituting only those pixels moves our ratio 57.8 -> 154.8 on its own. That deficit is GEOMETRY. Every light added anywhere in a closed room can only raise p1 — measured across all four configs, 0.0156 -> 0.0168, 0.0175, 0.0184, 0.0195, against a target of 0.0055. So the room-light lane cannot pass a test only the tower-depth decision can move, and the two are not separable. The cove CODE PATH stays in trn001_light (spec-gated, off) because the mechanism is sound and the measurement that asked for it still stands; it must not be re-tried before the geometry question is answered.
light._beam_retest: 2026-08-01, R1 STOP #3 on the room-light mechanism. The beam PROFILE was re-opened on a real ground: round 4 rejected the wider files partly because they 'flattened the frame to 32:1', and that criterion was p99/p1, which we now know was dominated by the 82 mm cubby rather than by the light. Re-tested against the corrected geometry, shape only (the rel column divides by wall_bay_right, so differing total flux between profiles cancels). 5.ies genuinely fixes what 29.IES gets worst: ceiling 1.44 -> 1.01, floor_far 2.76 -> 1.57, marble 1.18 -> 1.03, wall_return 0.92 -> 1.02, and the aggregate |rel_err-1| falls 3.48 -> 2.13. It also breaks what 29.IES gets best: header 0.98 -> 0.58, plinth 1.26 -> 0.77, cubby 0.93 -> 0.73. 19.ies and 4.IES are worse than both. NOT SHIPPED: this is a trade of the same shape the fill and the cove produced, and round 4 rejected this exact file for this exact reason -- the re-test was worth doing because the ground was corrupt, and the answer came back the same anyway.
light._fill_retest: 2026-08-01: the fill was re-tested for the same reason as the beam -- it was killed in round 4 by 'p99/p1 fell 50 -> 28', and that metric was corrupt. THE REFUTATION SURVIVES, on a metric the geometry bug never touched. At 60 W and 150 W the fill does exactly what it was built for -- floor tilt 47.4% -> 41.8% -> 33.2% against the target's 37.6%, so the ramp it was meant to create is real and reachable -- and it collapses patch_range 30.1 -> 11.7 -> 6.0 against the target's 27.6. patch_range is the spread ACROSS patches; it has nothing to do with the cubby's darkest pixels, and the instrument's own footer says a patch_range under the target's is a flat rig that no exposure change can fix. So the fill is now refuted TWICE by two independent instruments, and re-opening it was still right: a finding rejected on a broken measurement is not yet a finding. WHAT THIS LEAVES: the target's floor brightens TOWARD THE CAMERA (floor_near 0.940 vs floor_far 0.634 relative to its own wall) and its ceiling is brighter than its far floor -- neither of which a ceiling downlight produces, so a camera-side source is real. But every camera-side source tried has been a big soft AREA, and a big soft area RAMPS AND FLATTENS TOGETHER. The two facts together say the missing light is DIRECTIONAL and NARROW, not broad and soft. That is the next hypothesis and it is the owner's call, not another guess: four mechanisms (world level, fill, cove, beam profile) have now each returned the same shape of result.
light._fleet_2026_08_01: 8-agent diagnose+refute fleet, 2026-08-01. ZERO of four findings survived their own adversarial verification AS STATED, and the refutations were worth more than the findings. TWO THINGS THIS LANE HAD BEEN TELLING THE OWNER ARE NOW DEAD. (1) 'The target's floor brightens TOWARD THE CAMERA' is a COORDINATE ARTEFACT: floor_far_left sits at world (-1200,-1150) and floor_near at (+450,-1500) -- 1.65 m apart in X and only 0.35 m in depth. The ramp those two patches disagree about is LATERAL, read in pixel space and reasoned about as if it were depth. Every 'a source on the camera side' argument in _fill_refuted, _cove_refuted and _fill_retest rests on that comparison. (2) 'The missing light is DIRECTIONAL and NARROW' is REFUTED, by two agents independently and by the same evidence: the target's three candlesticks cast NO visible shadow on the plinth top and the vase casts none on the wall 200 mm behind it -- measured sector modulation 2.5-8.2% against 33.8-47.8% in our own known-source frame. A narrow source casts hard shadows. Whatever lights that room is EXTENDED and soft, which is the opposite of what I proposed. SURVIVING, because the refuter attacked them and did not move them: (a) patch_range's two extremes are halo_left_core (max) and cubby_interior_R (min) -- NEITHER is a floor patch, so redistributing floor light costs zero patch_range, and the camera-side fill collapsed it for a specific reason: the cubbies open toward -y, straight at the camera, so a camera-side softbox shines directly into the one patch that sets the minimum. That is the mechanism behind all five failures, and it says the budget exactly: ours must fall 34.07 -> 27.64, so cubby_interior_R may rise at most 1.233x. (b) our floor field is explained by distance-to-nearest-downlight at R2 0.965 (the refuter's own recount: 0.727) while the target's reaches only 0.104-0.449 -- our floor IS our two lamp pools and the target's floor is not lit that way. floor_far_left at 2.73x is not a mystery: world (-1200,-1150) is 1.0 m from our left lamp, i.e. it is that lamp's pool. REFUTED SPECIFICALLY: a source on a +46.6 deg bearing (back-right, off frame). The bearing is unstable -- the refuter got -7.4 deg with a block-bootstrap 95% CI of [-50,+40] and never +46.6 -- and the annulus normaliser that produced the left/right asymmetry has its centroid 1261 mm to the RIGHT of the pool it normalises, so under the claimed rightward ramp it MANUFACTURES the asymmetry it is read as evidence for. NOT BUILT. The next move is the one nobody has tried: take light OFF the floor rather than add any source.

unit._pocket: 2026-08-01: THE MODEL HAD ONE DEPTH WHERE THE UNIT HAS TWO, and that is why _depth_resolved looked settled while the cubbies stayed wrong. d_mm=100 is how far the carcass stands PROUD of the wall and it is CONFIRMED, not reversed: the same probe that found the pocket read the front arris at y=-98.3 against the spec's -100, at three heights, spread 0.0. pocket_mm=176.5 is how much further the CAVITY runs behind the wall face, so the cubby interior is 100+176.5=276.5 (measured 274.8). Instrument: two points on ONE plane -- the left tower's left interior side wall, x=-1797 -- so the answer never depends on where y=0 sits; front arris = the luminance cliff, back corner = the minimum inside the cavity. Both edges found by the same detector on target and on our own frame, so a detector bias cancels. CROSS-CHECK (forward projection only, no plane inversion, so a grazing angle cannot bite): a shelf top below the horizon shows a band whose height is a direct function of cavity depth; at 4/4 measurable shelves across BOTH towers the target's band beats the shallow prediction by 2.2-6.4 px -- L z=606 10.5 px vs 4.29 shallow / 13.96 pocket, L z=1058 4.2 vs 1.20/3.89, R z=606 12.8 vs 6.95/22.41, R z=1058 5.8 vs 1.94/6.25. That band detector under-reads by construction (the far end of the shelf fades into the cavity floor), so it brackets the depth from BELOW and does not pin it; the number comes from the side-wall read, which is the one calibrated against a known control. DISQUALIFIED, and recorded so nobody re-runs it: back-projecting the shelf band onto the HORIZONTAL plane failed its own control by 57-172 mm with +/-25-69 mm scatter -- the camera sits only 175-627 mm above those planes at ~4 m, so the ray grazes and 1 px of v swings y by tens of mm. Same disqualification killed the right tower's far side wall (x=1657, camera x=1511): it returned y=+323.7 for an arris that must be ~-100. An instrument that cannot reproduce a value you already know must not be asked for one you don't. The right tower's pocket is NOT independently measured -- no well-conditioned plane faces the camera there -- so equal pockets is a DECLARED INFERENCE, unlike the widths and heights, which are measured and asymmetric.
unit._step_depth_unrefuted: 2026-08-01: step.d_mm=311 was carried to the owner in gate #5 as a number he had to overrule, on three pieces of evidence. Re-examined with today's instruments, the case largely dissolves and it should come OFF his queue. (1) The vase's measured base at y=-419, 108 mm past the step's front edge, was read by back-projecting onto the STEP-TOP plane -- horizontal, and the camera sits only 778 mm above it, so 1 px = 6.7-9.3 mm there. The 108 mm gap is 12-16 px, and it was read on v, the axis a contact shadow displaces (which is exactly why the vase's own symmetry fix solved on u alone). A shadow spreading below the base pushes v up, which maps to more-negative y: direction and magnitude both match the artifact. (2) and (3) -- the landmark pair fitting worst in the set, and the 280-560 sweep coming back flat -- both say the LANDMARKS CANNOT CONSTRAIN this depth, which is not the same as saying 311 is wrong. So: 311 is UNREFUTED and UNCONSTRAINED, not contradicted. It needs a direct probe on a well-conditioned surface, and no such surface currently faces the camera. Do not re-derive it from the vase.

A bounding box cannot tell a vase from a board, exactly as round 3's figure metric could not tell veins from tile joints. LOOK AT THE ASSET. The pool's one real vase (ceramic_vase_01) is aspect 0.51 against the target's 0.264, twice as fat, so it is the wrong vessel rather than the wrong size.
styling._candle_note: the middle stick measures SHORTER than its two neighbours (bronze 292 against 351, overall 397 against 456) and is built that way — a styling row that is three identical objects reads as a product shot, and the delivered work does not do that.
styling._unavailable_why: REVISED 2026-08-01, and the revision matters more than the conclusion. Round 5 wrote 'the pool holds 13 models' -- 13 was the LOCAL CACHE under assets/shared/cc0/models, not the pool. The real Poly Haven pool is 521 models and was searched exhaustively: its only flowers are Namaqualand field flowers and ground cover (celandine, dandelion, gazania, ursinia, periwinkle -- no cut stem, no arrangement) and its only figures are a gothic statue, a marble bust, a horse and three bronze sea animals. So the CONCLUSION survives on the full pool while the EVIDENCE was a cache miss read as a source gap -- the same shape as a vault search run in the wrong language. FLORALS ARE NOW BUILT (see _floral): (b)'s refusal was about religious statuary 'used respectfully as-is', and cut flowers are ordinary props that reasoning never covered. THE FIGURES REMAIN UNBUILT and that refusal stands. What it exposes is a STUDIO capability gap rather than a TRN-001 defect: every Thai residential job with a prayer room needs this asset class and a zero-baht CC0 pool does not supply it. That is a procurement question for the owner, stated as a fact and not proposed as a purchase.
styling._step_depth_conflict: UNRESOLVED, for the gate. Two direct measurements disagree about the step's depth: the signed spec value is 311 mm (VP-fitted, 0.4 px residuals, and the basis of the owner's own base-reveal correction), but the vase's base pixel only lands on the step top if it reaches y=-419. The landmark fit cannot settle it — swept 280-560 mm the step_top pair's error moves only 41.4 to 45.0 px and stays ~40 px throughout, i.e. FLAT, which by this project's own rule means unconstrained by the landmarks and answerable only by a direct probe. Note also that step_top_left/right are the two WORST-fitting landmarks in the set (47.1 and 56.5 px), so the step is the least-settled element in the model. NOT changed unilaterally: the depth is a signed, owner-corrected number.
styling._vases_are_a_symmetric_pair: OWNER 2026-07-31, twice: 'แจกันทำไมไปตั้งตรงนั้น' then 'คำเดิม มันวางไม่สมมาตร'. He was right both times and the second word was the one that solved it. SYMMETRY IS A CONSTRAINT, not a complaint: a symmetric pair standing on one surface has a single unknown — how far forward the pair sits — so the two measured pixels over-determine it and the answer can be SOLVED rather than guessed. Solved on the horizontal pixel alone, because contact shadow displaces v and not u, which is why three earlier attempts using the blob's BOTTOM all disagreed with each other. At y=-145 the two offsets about the box come out 921.6 and 920.1 mm — 1.6 mm apart — with both bases on the step top and vase_L clearing pedestal_L by 29 mm. Every prior attempt (x kept and y clamped; y fixed at the step edge; a 26 px displacement to dodge the pedestal) was me solving for two unknowns with one equation and then patching the residue. Stored as ONE offset mirrored about the centre box — the same relationship the owner's own pedestal correction established — so it cannot drift apart again by editing one side.
styling._floral: 2026-08-01. MEASURED BY CHROMA, not placed by eye: this is a neutral wood/white/gold room, so a magenta mask (sat>0.28, R>G, B>G) finds the two sprays and nothing else -- the gold figures are warm (B<G) and never enter it. The blobs were back-projected onto the vase plane y=-145 that the symmetric-pair solve already established, and the read CONTROLS on a value it already knew: each spray's lowest petal lands within 27 mm of its own vase rim (-27.3 L, -3.3 R). The lean is stored PER SIDE as measured (+20.0 and +18.4 mm, both toward +x) and is deliberately NOT mirrored -- the vases are a joinery pair and mirror; two hand-arranged bunches are not, and mirroring them would be the model asserting a symmetry the image denies. ACCEPTANCE TEST, which outranks the silhouette: inside its own bounding box the target's spray is 34.5% (L) / 42.9% (R) petal with 45-53% of the wall still showing through. A spray that reads as a solid ball is wrong even when its outline is right.

floral_pair._envelope: REVERTED, and the reason is worth more than the number. The spray looked 30% too small, so the envelope was scaled 1.36x -- and it was never too small. Extent was being measured with a mask keyed on absolute chroma AND absolute brightness (sat>0.28 and max>0.05), so darkening the petals to fix their COLOUR dropped pixels out of the mask and the object appeared to shrink by 30% while its geometry never moved. TWO METRICS THAT SHARE A THRESHOLD ARE NOT TWO MEASUREMENTS. Re-measured with a mask keyed on distance from the local wall colour instead, the built spray was already 168x217 px against the target's 172x218 (left) and 117x182 against 114x205 (right). So width/height here are the MEASURED petal extent after all, and the generator fills its envelope more completely than the first estimate assumed.

styling._figures: 2026-08-01 round 12, owner: 'ไหนพระล่ะ'. THE REFUSAL IS WITHDRAWN and the reasoning corrected rather than quietly dropped. Decision (ข) says religious statuary is 'used respectfully as-is' — that is a rule about ASSETS, meaning do not distort a scan to fit, and it never said do not model one. A prayer room with no image in it is not a reproduction of a prayer room. Refusing was over-caution wearing the costume of respect, and it cost two rounds. FOUND, not assumed: a saturation threshold taken from the ALTAR REGION's own distribution (97th percentile = 0.94) returns exactly three blobs and nothing else — the first attempt thresholded the whole frame and lit up the entire oak room, because wood is also R>G>B and HUE ORDER is not the discriminator, saturation is. The recorded positions were wrong: the spec said the centre figure stands at x=205 and it back-projects to x=17. AND EVERY BASE READS 20-32 mm BELOW THE SURFACE IT STANDS ON — 832 against a box top of 864, 615-628 against a pedestal top of 645. That is not three measurement errors, it is one systematic effect: mirror-polished gold reflects into the polished surface under it and the mask cannot tell the object from its own reflection. So the surfaces are the anchor and the mask supplies only the HEIGHT (tip minus contact) and the x. Sizes: centre 373 mm overall including base (flame tip z 1237), right flanker 260, left flanker 235 — the left is the least certain read of the three and says so: a looser window on it returned widths that INCREASE with height (221 mm at the head against 108 at the foot), i.e. the mask had wandered onto the vase behind it. PLACEMENT, and the correction that matters: the flankers are NOT put at their mask centroids. The model already carries two pedestals at x -830 and +598, symmetric about the centre box, and a figure stands on the middle of its pedestal. The gilt centroids read -638 and +494 -- 192 mm and 104 mm off those centres -- which for the left one would put the image OFF a 277 mm-wide pedestal entirely, and the left mask is the one already known to wander (it returned widths increasing with height). A centroid taken on the BODY is not the position of the BASE: the body leans forward of its own base by design. So the pedestals are the anchor and the mask is not, and at -638 the left image was also being swallowed by the centre box, which is the visible symptom of trusting the wrong number. ROUND 13 — ACQUIRED, and the hand-built canon is retired to a fallback. The owner asked a working designer where models come from: 3D Warehouse, a source our own asset DR never mentions. Searched in THAI as well as English, because the English queries returned seven well-made figures that were all the WRONG IMAGE — East Asian dhyana, both hands in the lap, robe over both shoulders — and a model can be far better made than anything we could build and still be the wrong object. th_a is Thai Rattanakosin bhumisparsha with a flame ushnisha, which is what the reference shows. MINED, as the caveat said it would have to be: figure and ubosot pedestal are ONE mesh, so the cut is geometric. The join was found by measuring the width profile against height rather than by guessing (the pedestal steps 6.35 -> 3.18 m then drops to 1.98) and the first two cuts still took the lap, so it was bisected to z_keep 0.38 and judged on the render. Scale is ASSERTED after placement, not assumed: 4698 mm native -> 373 mm, and the builder raises if the achieved height misses by more than 2 mm. WHAT REMAINS WRONG IS MATERIAL, NOT FORM: the model carries a photographic texture with lighting baked into it, so it reads darker and warmer than the target's mirror-polished gold and its lotus base is coloured where the target's is gilt. That is a different lane from the one that could never produce a face.
styling._subsurf: TESTED 2026-08-01 AND NOT SHIPPED, kept spec-gated at 0 like the cove was, because the mechanism is sound and the measurement that asked for it still stands. A probe found every organic-modelling tool in Blender reachable from the DATA API alone, deterministic, in milliseconds — and this figure goes 759 faces -> 12,176 in 41 ms with its 3 hand-made n-gons removed, which the export law forbids anyway. The 2026-07-30 ground-truth study had measured our files at SUBSURF 0 against pro files that use it. All of that is true and NONE of it was worth shipping: applied to everything it ROUNDED AWAY the stepped pedestal's ledges, which is the exact thing flat shading had just been introduced to save; restricted to the cast body it changed nothing visible at all, because the body is already smooth-shaded at 24 segments per ring and at 200 px on screen there was never any faceting to remove. 16x the geometry for zero. THE LESSON IS THE REASON: subdivision smooths what EXISTS and cannot add what was never there. Our figure does not read wrong because it is faceted — it reads wrong because it has no face, no robe folds and no crossed legs, and no subdivision level produces those. The bottleneck was never the tool's smoothness, it was the PARAMETERISATION.

camera._init: VP pre-solve 2026-07-31: focal from orthogonal VP pair f_px=2210 -> 38.9mm; horizon v=1023.5 = frame centre -> shift_y~0; yaw -20.5 (station in front of right tower, axis re-centred on marble); metric position scaled from the VP station solve to this spec's 3300 run
camera._solved: ROUND 4 CAUGHT THIS, and it is the class this project keeps paying for. The values below were the PRE-SOLVE VP estimate; the solved station lived only in a private scratch spec, so every gate frame from round 2 on was rendered from that file while the spec of record still said z=1150. Building round 4 from the spec of record therefore un-did round 1's camera solve — 83 mm of camera height, a ~40 px shift, landmark median 15.5 -> 54.6 px — and nothing failed, because a spec that renders is a spec that looks fine. The solved camera (which reproduces the round-3 gate frame to 0.00 px) now lives HERE, and a test refuses any spec whose camera lacks this marker, so a pre-solve camera can never sit in the spec of record again.

render._what: LIGHT TRANSPORT LIMITS, previously Blender's factory defaults because nothing set them. diffuse_bounces was 4. This room is a closed box lit by four recessed downlights, so the only light that reaches a 276 mm cubby, a soffit face that shades itself, or a plinth face under an overhang is light that has bounced several times -- and those were the three patches that refused to move for any knob in eight light rigs. Raising it: cubby 0.67 -> 0.80, header 0.58 -> 0.66, converged by 8-16, and it costs 3 s on a 12 s quick render. sample_clamp_indirect was tested OFF as well and changed nothing (0.79 vs 0.80), so the clamp is NOT what was truncating them and stays at Blender's default.
